news.title: 漫威对手的创意总监解决了仇恨言论争议，并承诺“我们已经加强了纪律措施”
news.summary: A September incident that saw hate speech removed from the game's reporting system "sparked massive controvers

content.v: A few months ago Marvel Rivals became embroiled in one of the biggest controversies in its history when an error during an update ended up removing the "Hate Speech" option in its reporting system. This unfortunately led to a huge rise in slurs and hate speech within the game, and it also damaged the relationship between NetEase and players as many felt the studio wasn't doing enough to provide adequate safeguards for players .

Little was said about the issue at the time, although it was corrected fairly quickly and NetEase promised harsher penalties for toxic behaviour a few weeks later. Now Marvel Rivals' creative director Guangyun Chen has explained what exactly went wrong and what the team is doing to rectify the issue in a recent dev diary :
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/63JKawy8iZa6eETcv3EjVP-1920-80.png

"In mid September, while optimising our report system UI, we made a configuration error that caused the 'Hate Speech' option to be replaced by 'Crime'. The moment we discovered the issue, we fixed it immediately—it was an oversight on our part."

Mistakes happen, but what matters more is that NetEase is now trying to do more to combat hate speech in Marvel Rivals. "This incident sparked massive controversy in the community, and we realised right then that simply fixing a UI option wouldn't be enough to combat hate speech," Guangyun Chen says. "Because of this, we've entirely overhauled our penalty system for abusive language."

Starting on September 24, NetEase "ramped up our disciplinary measures," meaning that the "most severe offenders" will be met with a 365-day chat ban, something that players are overjoyed to see enacted . But he still reminds players that a healthy game environment also depends on the players—yeah, that's the problem.
"We strongly encourage everyone to report any toxic behaviour immediately," Guangyun Chen adds. "Our operations team verifies every report to ensure the appropriate penalties are applied."

news.title: 有 Synology NAS 吗？是时候检查您的更新了，因为两个高级漏洞可让不熟练者读写文件并进行 DDOS 攻击
news.summary: Big oof.

content.v: Another day, another cybersecurity update. This time, it's the turn of immensely popular NAS provider Synology to advise its users about some now-fixed gaping holes. The company has updated its DiskStation Manager (DSM) operating system , patching out two security vulnerabilities in various product versions.

Just another patch? Not quite. The first of these vulnerabilities has a CVSS3 base score of 9.8 out of 10, which makes it of "critical" severity (via International Cyber Digest on X ). According to the company:

"An improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command vulnerability in the Auth API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM)... allows remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks."

That's a pretty big security hole if I've ever seen one, particularly for those storing extremely important data on their home NAS setup. The second one gets a lower severity rating of 8.6, but also manages to allow attackers to skip the login process.

Synology describes the second vulnerability as "An authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the rsync in Synology DiskStation Manager," which can again lead to unwanted reads, writes, and DDOS shenanigans.

‼️BREAKING: A critical flaw in Synology NAS devices lets attackers read and write any file on them without logging in.The SQL injection bug in their login system scores 9.8 out of 10. A second flaw, in rsync, skips the login too.Synology patched both today. Update ASAP. https://t.co/LlS328SBf4 November 11, 2026

The company also notified users late last month of ransomware attacks related to a 2024 security advisory , for what looks to be a series of separate vulnerabilities. One way or the other, the latest updates look to have rolled out to many users already, but it's still worth checking to make sure you're on the newest builds to plug all these leaks.

After all, auto updaters are far from perfect. 2026 has been a year characterised by cybersecurity issues, and it'd really put the tin lid on it if your home NAS was broken into by some unscrupulous character. A reminder to keep on top of your updates no matter the device, methinks. Stay safe out there, folks.

news.title: 前《铁拳》总监在 Xbox 高级员工面前猛烈抨击 Xbox Series S：“感觉就像必须为一个稍弱的孩子做额外的工作”
news.summary: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say 'Xbox Series S sucks,' right?"

content.v: Ex-Tekken director and current SNK VS Studio CEO Katsuhiro Harada expressed some sheer savagery at the Console Game Developers Conference in Seoul a couple of days ago. According to Inven Global , the game director and producer slated the Xbox Series S right in front of a "senior Xbox official" (via EuroGamer ).

Harada said: "there's something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the 'Xbox Series S' wouldn't be released (laughs). I want to ask Director Paweł personally—honestly, weren't you upset inside because of Series S?"
He's talking to CDPR Associate Game Director Paweł Sasko, who reportedly bursts out laughing and responds: "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly."
Harada: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say 'Xbox Series S sucks,' right?"

The reason, which Harada continues to explain, is that despite the Series S being more popular than Series X in the US, low memory is an issue and its performance is "awkwardly lower" than the Series X: "With Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child."

Sasko actually agrees, although he puts a positive spin on it: "Harada speaks a lot of truth... However, intensely optimizing for lower-spec platforms definitely brings the benefit of making the game run significantly better across all platforms—including PS5, high-end PCs, and handhelds like Steam Deck and ROG Ally... And the biggest advantage of Series S is that its affordable price makes it accessible."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cp6jZSR8vj5Z6cz2mBrewm-1920-80.jpg

Harada: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)."

As savage as it is for Harada to point all this out in front of an Xbox rep, it's not wrong. We recently saw, for instance, that Rockstar is targeting just 30 fps for GTA 6 on PlayStation and Xbox . That's "while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life", apparently.

We PC gamers, on the other hand—the refined and exemplary folk that we are—can enjoy frame rates just as high as our systems allow. Which is, err, actually not so much given the ridiculous hardware prices of late. Let's just forget about that and remain smug, shall we?

news.title: Steam 不断增加的审核积压导致另一款游戏的发布日期被推迟
news.summary: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is

content.v: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is stuck in the purgatory of the platform's review program. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business , a post-apocalyptic game about keeping a cargo railway running after society has collapsed, was originally scheduled to launch on November 10, but it's stuck waiting for Steam's mandatory QA review before it can be published.

"Unfortunately, we're stuck waiting for Steam to review and approve our launch build. We have been waiting for a few weeks now and sadly don't know when they will finally get around to it," Australia Did It publisher Mystic Forge wrote in an update. "We're hoping to be able to launch as soon as possible and will update all of you the second we get an update. We really appreciate all of your continued support and apologize for the situation. We can't wait for you to check out the final game and hope to be able to get it into your hands soon!"

Australia Did It co-developer and game designer Rami Ismail said the game was originally submitted on October 20, and a minor controller issue caused it to fail. That bug was fixed the same day, but since then, Ismail and Aesthecian Labs have been stuck waiting for Steam approval.

"We've been in the queue again ever since, and have followed up with Valve several times to no result," Rami explained in an email to GameSpot. "The issue was that our in-game feedback functionality does not allow you to send feedback--from a keyboard text input--via controller. I'm used to this kind of hold-and-wait pattern on console, but not really on Steam. 10-14 days pre-launch is usually enough to fail twice over, and usually you only get failed on serious issues."

With reviews for Australia Did It already out, and the game on plenty of wishlists, not having it ready for its scheduled launch isn't doing it any favors. "Pre-emptively delaying the launch would've hurt, as did not doing so," Ismail added. "We decided to take that gamble and trust in Valve's willingness to come through for developers - it seems we bet wrong."

Is a deluge of AI slop to blame for Australia Did It being stuck in QA limbo? Ismail explained that Steam can set its own policies and host "slopware" games on its own servers, but it's also having a negative effect on developers.

"At 30% off of every game sold on the platform, I have to admit I don't really care what the reason is. It's likely slopware is a part of the issue, but the fact that slopware can exist on Steam is their own policy. Whatever the situation, Steam losing the agility and access for developers to launch with minimal friction will mean developers have to treat it more like a console - which means we have to be more careful about launches."

While releasing the game on another platform like the Epic Games Store could be one solution, Ismail noted that the "commercial potential" is much lower than on Steam, which accounts for the lion's share of PC game sales. "With Epic, we're just trading the one billionaire for the other, and the commercial potential is also much lower. For now we're stuck with Steam for commercial game releases."

Ordinarily, every game submitted to Steam undergoes a series of checks to ensure that it'll work on the launcher, a process that used to take a few days. Lately, multiple developers have been complaining that this process now takes up to two weeks, and in some instances, longer, as Steam is reportedly battling to work through a backlog of submitted games. Several studios have blamed a flood of AI slop games, which regularly fail QA and are then resubmitted for review, gumming up the works and creating a bottleneck.

Recently, Valve introduced new measures to help speed up the process, but it's unclear if they've had any real impact. Under the new guidelines, games submitted for QA are required to be run through the Steam launcher for a minimum of five minutes; there will be stricter enforcement on images so that players aren't misled; Steam will run automated checks to flag broken or incomplete achievements; and advertised features will need to be included.

news.title: 《黑暗之魂 2》和《黑暗之魂 3》多人游戏回归：我们仍然不知道出了什么问题，但至少没有花近一年的时间来修复它
news.summary: A "server issue" knocked both games offline, across all platforms, for nearly two weeks.

content.v: A little less than two weeks after their multiplayer features were taken offline because of a mysterious " server issue ," multiplayer functionality in Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 has been restored, meaning invasions and messages are once again working as they should.

Word of the service restoration game via a very businesslike message on the Dark Souls website: "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored.
"We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding."

So what exactly went wrong? Well, that's the mysterious part. Aside from intermittent apologies for the inconvenience and thanks for your patience in messages posted to X, FromSoft's had nothing to say about it—and that remains the case now: It's back, be happy, speak of the matter no more.

Whatever happened, it clearly wasn't as serious a problem as the 2022 mess that saw PC servers for all Dark Souls games shut down for the better part of a year . In that case, FromSoft copped to the problem: A security vulnerability that allowed malicious code to be executed via the games' online services. But that fix was also long in coming because FromSoft was busy with other things, like finishing Elden Ring , which was kind of a big deal.

Anyway, aside from the relative brevity of the downtime, we had something else that made the outage a little more bearable than it was back in '22: The Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 Seamless Co-op mods that operate independently of FromSoft's servers. They also enable a far more flexible multiplayer experience than what's offered by the games themselves, letting players team up to run through the games at will, and without having to deal with disconnects when somebody dies or a boss gets smoked.
But if your preference is for the chaos of native Dark Souls multiplayer? Now that option's back on the table too.

news.title: 安钛克 C6 Curve Air 评测
news.summary: A chassis that ticks all the right boxes at just the right price.

content.v: Shangri-la, the promised land. Aside from the very notion of that concept being oh so appetising in the chaotic world that is 2026, there's something of that in the C6 Curve Air. An odd way to start a chassis review, I'll admit, particularly one that genuinely, I think is probably one of the best PC cases of 2026, but it's more than a metaphor here.

This feels like something a little special this case. It feels like how Corsair's 4000D series felt, or NZXT's H7 lineup when that first debuted, or even Phanteks' Evolv arsenal from way back when at the start of my tech journalism career. There's something iconic here, that I can't quite place my finger on, something that I think is massively underrated in the world of custom rigs. Refined subtlety.
Honestly the C6 Curve Air feels as if it's some bastard love child of the Phanteks Evolv series, Asus's Pro Art line and Fractal Design's North variants. Born in secret, and somehow less than $100.

It's clean, modest, with an elegant aesthetic, good choice of materials, dependable internal layout, decent cable management, and it's genuinely a chassis that I can't stop looking at. It's not flawless, nothing ever is, but what Antec has done here is, particularly in a market that's so over saturated with tempered glass black obelisks, is impressive.
Buy if...

✅ You want a budget, clean chassis that stands out from the crowd: With curved tempered glass, a stylish base, and a remarkably crisp interior at an outstanding price point the C6 Curve Air, is one of the best looking affordable cases you can find on the market today.
Don't buy if...

✅ You're using a massive graphics card: Bells and whistles are minimal in the C6 Curve Air to save on cost of manufacturing, which means there's no anti-sag bracket included. If you're using a larger triple-slot, pick up an aftermarket anti-sag mount elsewhere.
Antec C6 Curve Air - features

At a surface level, there's not a huge amount to talk about here in terms of overall featureset. It's a typical mid-tower case, it's got support for ATX, there's some nice rubber grommets built in to hide the cables protruding from the rear, it's got a full PSU shroud, and some fairly modest fan and rad mounting locations dotted around the place, and well that's about it. The big standout feature is of course, the tempered glass. It's curved along the front edges, and wraps around midway back through the rear of the chassis, but there's no special innovative, screaming from the rooftops technical element at play here.

That glass is a curious decision as well, because it cuts your case cable management space down in half, and there's no additional intake mounting points either, nor front nor side, other than the two (included) 120 mm fans situated in the floor itself.

But here's the thing with the C6 Curve Air. These small seemingly mundane features that it has, that we've seen in cases for the last ten years, are so well refined, that it's almost like a complete fresh launch.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HDML9M2hPJh4J5gEsrsvXT-1920-80.jpg

Take the intake fans. They're twin 120 mm reverse blade designs, recessed into the floor of the PSU shroud. Now, that's a space usually taken up by a hard drive caddy (which very few of us use), and an abundance of excess stuffed cables. To counter that, Antec's opted for no caddy there at all, leaving one mounting location on the back of the CPU tray, and redesigned the entire PSU area, so it's rotational by its nature.

You can slot a 160 mm PSU in here, sideways, with a power lead passthrough, and route all the cables directly up the back of the motherboard tray. No need for a Corsair RMx Shift here, no sir, any old PSU will do. That means, cable management routes are remarkably direct, and there's little mess to manage or tight corners to wrap your cables around.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RBfbhmg58bpQK9pacrLsMT-1920-80.jpg

As for the actual cable management, there's not a mad amount of support here either. There's a few velcro straps, and three plastic clips on the right, and those rubber grommets and that's it, but it's enough, and if you tuck your extra SATA cables out of the way, those twin 120 mm intakes have plenty of space to pull air up and through. It's actually one of the cleanest cable managed cases I've built, and there's not a single tie in sight.

Both sides, and the entire base of the chassis are well ventilated as well, with either that pristine slat design lining the front and edges, or pure perforations, so cool airflow is ample. It's all just very well thought out.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/BfGfHifrTzpPtMNuaDPvXT-1920-80.jpg

The only thing that mildly irked me, was a lack of a removable radiator bracket, (which would've made subsequent cable management at the end considerably easier), and there's no GPU anti-sag bracket either, which has almost become a staple in modern designs.
Antec C6 Curve Air - Value
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hsaABQQmKcXGYAVPRTXwXT-1920-80.jpg

And that's all coming in at just around the $100 mark, if not cheaper. Antec, also has a white variant available too, for a little extra if you do fancy something a bit punchier in terms of the overall aesthetic.

There are alternatives out there, that allow you to fit more kit in, mount more fans etc, but few cases feel quite as good as what you're getting here. Hyte's Y40 is a good example, or Lian Li's O11 Vision Compact .

And of course you can get some flashier cases as well, Phanteks' XT View Matrix with its full dot grid display, again fits in that groove. But none of them feel particularly timeless compared to this.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/65hjug3LYBkGpaUCpVuawS-1920-80.jpg

There is one caveat to all of this of course, and that's long term future viability here. Although the case design itself will last for many years to come, let's say hypothetically RAM and silicon manufacturing ramp up by 300% in the next two years somehow, and datacenter demand drops (we can only hope), and you do want to build a new machine with new more power hungry hardware, I do have some concern that those twin 120 mm intakes, might not be quite enough to cool both a thirsty GPU and CPU combo longer into the future.
Antec C6 Curve Air - Aesthetics
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ieEjmJvDfkeqW99SmG445T-1920-80.jpg

I've waxed lyrically about how this thing looks visually already, but it's worth stressing because it's a thing of beauty. There is absolutely something "ProArty" about the C6 Curve Air. Even if it's just its design philosophy. The slats, the power button, the understated lack of lighting, the curved glass. It's undeniably luscious in scope. Heck even that roof panel, slimline, compact, smooth against the top just sings to the overall design, and that blend of perforated mesh around the PSU area, sits strikingly against the slats feeding the intake fans, and it really stands out.

It's overall a little wider than you'd think for a mid-tower, particularly given the height (in part to accommodate the rotated PSU), but given we've got so many cuboid styled dual chamber cases these days, I'm not opposed to a little extra girth (don't quote me on that).

content.v: A step in the right direction?

After being leaked earlier this week, the European Commission has today presented its proposal for the ' Digital Fairness Act ' — a rule update that aims to offer "better protection for consumers and fairer competition for businesses" in the games industry.

To be clear, the proposal has not been adopted by the EU Commission just yet, but if it does go through, it could have a huge impact on several hot-topic game mechanics like loot boxes, virtual currencies, pay-to-win options and more. What's more, the act would apply to all EU member states without the need for individual approval.

news.title: 贝塞斯达设定了粉丝对《上古卷轴 VI》的期望：今日哨兵新闻
news.summary: Bethesda has issued an official response to fans expecting a major announcement for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sent

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/theelderscrolls6-sentinel-blogroll-1793718530021.jpg
Bethesda has issued an official response to fans expecting a major announcement for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel at some point today.

In a post from the company's official account on reddit , Bethesda said it had seen the growing speculation among its fans that today, November 11, would bring more details on Sentinel, hot on the heels of the game's subtitle and logo reveal just last week .
Alas, today will not be when we find out more about the game, Bethesda has now said — pouring cold water on hopes that we would see more of the Hammerfell-set role-player anytime soon.

Despite being announced eight years ago, Sentinel is reportedly still two years away from launch — at least . We don't even know which platforms it will launch on (could it be an Xbox Helix launch title?) or whether it will be an Xbox console exclusive . Of course, that hasn't stopped Bethesda already beginning to sell Sentinel merch .

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," Bethesda wrote overnight (tomorrow meaning today, November 11). "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time."

Response to that statement is unsurprisingly a little mixed, with some fans commenting that they appreciate the clarity from Bethesda, while others joking that it will be another eight years before we see anything more of the game.

Of course, November 11 is an important date in the minds of The Elder Scrolls fans. It is the original release date for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, all the way back in 2011 (memorably, on 11/11/11). 15 years on, you can see why some had hoped Bethesda might have more to say today — but alas that is not set to be the case.

For those wanting to read more Sentinel today, however, IGN has you covered. We've got a deep dive on what Sentinel actually means based on The Elder Scrolls lore , and why Sentinel's in-universe quote teaser is sparking particular timeline speculation . We also have a roundup of former Bethesda design director Bruce Nesmith's wishes for Sentinel , whenever the long-awaited game does finally arrive.

news.title: Kioxia 将 640 个 SSD 连接在一起，创建了 157 *PB* 存储解决方案，因为 AI 数据中心拥有所有炫酷玩具
news.summary: Got any spare gigabytes, guv?

content.v: There's a golden rule of storage: no matter how much you have, it's never quite enough. Nevertheless, Kioxia is taking that principle to its limits, as it's announced " a new storage density milestone " in the form of 640 of its 245.76 TB enterprise SSDs chained together to create just over 157 petabytes worth of storage in a single rack cabinet.
157 petabytes is... well, it's 157 million gigabytes. Enough storage space for God of War: Ragnarok, a 190 GB game , to be installed over 820,000 times.

And yes, it's been designed for AI data centers. The "storage solution" (I do hate that term) has been created in collaboration with Dell, and essentially amounts to 16 PowerEdge R7725xd servers , each stuffed with 40 Kioxia LC9 Series drives inside one industry-standard 42U server rack .

"As AI workloads drive continued growth in unstructured data, organizations need storage that can deliver higher capacity without a corresponding increase in data center floor/rack space, power consumption or cooling requirements," says the press gumph. "High-capacity NVMe SSDs can help address these demands by consolidating more data into a smaller, more efficient infrastructure footprint."

Which seems timely. With physical data center size becoming an increasing issue (not least because massive data center buildouts are a tad unpopular right now), cramming as much storage as possible into a single rack is sure to save on some concrete, at the very least.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KVW5oMDYNFxDeCiTCXUzWA-1920-80.jpg

But I'm not going to suggest this sort of excessive consumption is anything but jarring, given us little ol' consumers are counting our pennies in the middle of a NAND flash crisis . Have you seen the price of game-ready SSDs recently? I have. It ain't pretty.

But hey, at least we know where 157 petabytes-worth of raw flash capacity is going. Straight into one of these rack cabinets, where it can be used for all sorts of AI-related purposes. The sometimes-intelligent beast needs feeding, and Kioxia and Dell appear to have worked very hard to fit its lunch inside one handy box.

news.title: 暴雪改变了《魔兽世界》高等级任务的永久金币奖励，玩家们正在庆祝
news.summary: For the longest time in World of Warcraft, when you finished a quest at max level, the experience you would ea

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/03/mxr-wowforever-promofi-1793722551273.png

For the longest time in World of Warcraft, when you finished a quest at max level, the experience you would earn would get converted to gold. But in WoW Forever, Blizzard killed off that conversion, and has now added a fix.

The experience-to-gold conversion for quests completed at high level has been a part of WoW for nearly 20 years, to the point where a lot of players rely on it to build up some cash when they hit max level, especially in the Classic versions of the game. But, when WoW Forever launched last week, that conversion was missing, and now that players are starting to hit level 60, they're starting to feel that loss of gold.

Thankfully, Blizzard community manager Kaivax has posted on the WoW forum to say a hotfix will go live "in the next 24 hours or so" to help high level players earn a little bit of gold. Rather than converting experience to gold, Blizzard will buff the gold rewarded for high level quests, regardless of what level you are.

According to Kaivax: "we’re preparing a hotfix that will add additional gold rewards to most quests with a quest level of level 48 or higher, including adding gold to quests above level 48 that never previously rewarded gold at all. The idea here is that you should feel good about doing quests at the appropriate level to progress your character, and you should feel adequately rewarded with gold for doing so."

But why change that experience-gold conversion in the first place? Well, according to Kaivax, that conversion "created an incentive for players to hold a full quest log worth of completed quests to hand in after hitting level 60 for maximum gold returns. Under those conditions, the optimal way for players to level to 60 was to simply grind creatures for XP and not hand in quests at all, which is not a design we want to retain in WoW: Forever."

Kaivax's post was in a thread where players were complaining about not being able to earn gold from quests. The original post was from Faze, who said four days ago that "the change to not give additional gold in exchange for EXP at 60 needs to be reverted. Quests are basically useless at 60 if they don’t have a reward. This was one of the easy ways to make gold to afford spells and mounts. This is a horrible design and change. It feels good to complete quests and now this just feels BAD at 60. Change this back ASAP."

Before Kaivax posted, nearly 100 replies deep, there were a ton of players who were essentially saying that they'd stop playing the game over this. Player Glôwstick said: "this is a deal breaker for me, wont be playing any more until this is reverted," while Rackjaw commented: "WoW Forever devs seem to be obsessed with 'fixing' things that aren’t broken."

However, players seem to have changed their tune immediately after Kaivax's response. Danni said: "Nice change. Quests giving consistent gold whether you do them at 59 or 60 makes sense, and doesn’t punish people for handing them in 'too soon.'"

There are some players that are skeptical about the change. For instance, Jalesanda posted: "I will withhold putting the pitch forks away for now until we see how much gold this is, and how it compares. But it’s put down, for now."

This change really does highlight the philosophy that the WoW Forever team is taking with the new game mode, though. While there are players who probably want a 1:1 copy of Classic, Forever will make changes as long as they stay within the 'spirit' of the game. That's why, for instance, the devs held the line on group tagging , but had no problem adding some quests like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' or changing how dungeon experience is earned.

And as more players start to reach max level , the initial design of WoW Forever is going to be pushed to its limits, and we'll just have to see the extent of changes that Blizzard is going to be willing to make. Right now, WoW Forever is kind of like a blank canvass, and while I've been given some hints of where the game might go in the future, I can't wait to see the unique path Forever takes. And this experience to gold conversion change is really just the first of many changes I'm sure we're going to see.

news.title: 《最终幻想 14》玩家聚集在虚拟守夜活动中，纪念游戏中最负盛名的贝斯手的去世
news.summary: The Primals' Eikichi Iwai has died at the age of 57.

content.v: Final Fantasy 14 players have been gathering en masse across servers today in the wake of the news that Eikichi Iwai—the bassist behind the game's band The Primals—has passed away at the age of 57.

A post went out on The Lodestone in the early hours of this morning (November 11) which read: "Thank you very much for your continued support of The Primals. As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eBdSMeeGWcMCQSCbS6T4Sn-1920-80.jpg

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.
"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."
The Primals is Final Fantasy 14's in-house band, fronted by composer Masayoshi Soken and localisation lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and accompanied by Tetsuya Tachibana, GUNN, and Iwai himself.

Iwai's bass in particular has elevated a ton of already-excellent tracks across the game's history: Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze, Shadowbringers' To the Edge, Endwalker's Scream and Close in the Distance, and Dawntrail's Ride the Rhythm just to name a few. The Primals has just come off the back of a strong year for live performances, too—from their usual appearance at all three Fan Festivals that took place this year, to even taking the stage at the UK's biggest rock and music festival as part of Download's lineup .

A quick trip through some of Final Fantasy 14's European servers have seen tons of players gathering in main hubs like Limsa Lominsa to pay their respects and share what it is about Iwai's work that meant so much to them. As I write this story, players and campfires line the perimeter of Omega's Limsa Lominsa plaza—a common practice for honouring the passing of key community figures and beyond, something which I've previously witnessed for the likes of Berserk's creator Kentaro Miura and Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama.
It's a small gesture, but one which is a pleasant reminder of why Final Fantasy 14 continues to maintain such an iron grip on myself and many others.

news.title: 不再需要在 Google 搜索末尾加上“reddit”，因为 Reddit 评论可以汇集每个人的想法
news.summary: Prepare for the review bombing.

content.v: I'm no stranger to slapping "Reddit" on the end of a Google search about a product to see what the unwashed masses (myself included) think about it. Assuming we're not reading bot comments, it's a great way to get a feel for a product you've not tested yourself. That's traditionally involved trawling various threads yourself, but now 'Reddit Reviews' is launching , which will collect user opinions on products and use them to inform dedicated reviews for them on Reddit's site.

"Today, we are starting to test Reddit Reviews, a new experience that organizes product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews and highlights the most important takeaways from across our communities. With Reddit Reviews, people can now more easily understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them."

AI is involved, of course: "Reddit Reviews uses AI to both organize these conversations where people describe their product experiences, and to surface the nuance, context, and connection to the original conversation."

Once it rolls out to you, you'll be able to search Reddit for reviews or for categories of products, and you'll also be able to navigate to relevant categories and similar products from the review you're looking at. In each review, you'll be shown the ratio of positive, mixed, or negative conversations about the product, as well as peoples' likes and dislikes, and you'll be able to filter in/out what's most relevant to you.
There's another aspect to this, too—a monetary one: "Many reviews also include images, prices, and purchase links where supplied by brand and retailer catalogs."
Presumably that will be an affiliated link that gives Reddit some small percentage of of any money spent, though I can't say for sure. If so, this could be another crucial revenue stream for Reddit.

While Reddit Reviews is only rolling out to US iOS users over the coming weeks and will cover around 10,000 products, the company says, "Throughout 2027, we plan to add more products and categories to Reddit Reviews and expand beyond the US."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fQQZeVrvg4mDuZJAHSuuqZ-1920-80.jpg

Speaking of the elephant in the room, though—the possibility that people could be steered to Reddit for these amalgamated reviews rather than to sites like yours truly—I'm not too concerned. People already go to Reddit to check out user opinions on products; I do the same. I don't think collecting all those opinions up will change much in that regard, only make it a bit easier to do. It's a good move, I reckon.

Though how it pans out in practice is an open question. There's a chance, for instance, that it could open the door to review bombing. If enough people hate a company, for instance, they could band together to write badly about a product and then get its 'official' amalgamated Reddit review looking negative.
I'll be interested to see how (or if) Reddit deals with such things, as well as the opposite: companies using bots to speak highly of their own products.

news.title: 数独SK700V评测
news.summary: If all air towers were built like this, I'd probably never use an AIO.

content.v: Where do I even begin with this thing? I'm so conflicted on the SK700V. It's such a unique problem, simultaneously excellent, and yet surprisingly frustrating to talk about. I'll start with the positive. It's exceptional. For the price, the display, the cooling, the installation process, it's next level, and I've never seen anything like it. It's honestly impressive. Without a doubt, the best air cooler I've tested in years.
But, even with that glowing accolade there, boy does it irritate me.

Let's talk features first, though, before I start to wail on the minor inconveniences that have upset my tech media brain, because the SK700V has one pretty nifty detail straddling its heatpipes, and that's namely, a full-fat display gracefully sitting atop that shiny tower.

Yep, it's a screen we've finally got them folks, air towers with screens on them. And if Computex is anything to go by this year, we're going to be seeing a lot more screens on things. Graphics cards, CPU towers, heck, I'd be surprised if we don't see them on DRAM soon. That'll bring the price down, I'm sure of it.
Buy if...
✅ You want an affordable, compatible CPU tower with a display: Compatible with practically all RAM kits imaginable, with exceptional performance, and a display as standard, all for sub $100. Nice.
Don't buy if...
✅ You're running hotter chips: It's solid, but don't expect it to cool your overclocked Core i9 14900K, or AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D. If that's the case you'll still want a beefy AIO behind them.
Type
Single-tower
Dimensions
Heatpipes
7 x 6 mm
Compatibility
AM5, AM4, (LGA1851, LGA1700, LGA1200, LGA115X, with mounting kit)
Fans
1x 120 mm
Price

It's not your full-fat OLED display, or anything fancy, but rather a simple digital-clock style system that actively reports on CPU frequency, temp, load, and power draw all on the fly. There's not much in the way of customisation in the software, but to be honest, there doesn't really need to be.
Sudokoo's generally quite an interesting company too. It's relatively new, founded in 2024, and is working in collaboration with a Taiwanese OEM with designs that remind me a lot of DeepCool's.
The SK700V is remarkably affordable for a licensed design. Sudokoo's pitching the SK700V at around $90 in the US and £80 in the UK, which is remarkably affordable given what you're getting here.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/t8KDhUkU47YdqKKTYLzG9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/YYdLUijupFfV53LLUbTd8k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4tVrzE8L89q6u5aa3hgL9k-1920-80.jpg
I'm going to cover the irritating bits now, actually, because I want to get them out of the way, as genuinely there's a lot of good to talk about here.

Unboxing the SK700V is a real experience. The packaging is lush, pink and yellow. You open it up, and inside, in my case, there are two kits, an included Intel mounting bracket kit (which, annoyingly, Sudokoo sell separately), and a severe lack of thermal paste (although bizarrely, you do get some grease cleaner).

I don't understand why these two things are not included by default. I know that's a weird hill to die on, but there's literally zero reason why they shouldn't be included. This isn't some specially designed Noctua NH-L9i where the mounting is built directly into the low-profile frame.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Nxw2AgBTagNyGTqnZWEQ9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4tVrzE8L89q6u5aa3hgL9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vNiYkzPksvqUYZQ7huBM9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/SWs4J2BqTwvKYnJno73Y9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/tq4JRTNUrTT7EKJcbpoCAk-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MGxs5jFaqmUAnPryHfqM9k-1920-80.jpg

This is a standard run-of-the-mill air-tower (albeit a very slim one), so why that Intel bracket isn't included is beyond me. Intel isn't dead, come on, guys. Oh, and the thermal paste too. Please, we're talking cents here, pennies, sweet naff all, include a tiny tube.

Installing it, though, was perhaps the most seamless experience I've ever had. Get your brackets set up, then take your tower, and slide the fan up and out of its rails (yes, rails). Underneath, you'll see some contact points for the display, and a hole for the included long screw driver on the back side. The front screw mount is easily reachable by any standard model. Then, once you're mounted, just slide the fan back in, clicking it into place, plug in the cables, and you're good to go. No funky, annoying metal clips, no awkward mounts, it's just brilliant. It's also remarkably compact; even with the fan in place, I could easily install memory after, no problem.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bzrEDX5aYqcJuDEXCD8a9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RAQ7XXk5PwbNrSAJkZNW9k-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Udno7uRhmzbCCBSTuGpQ9k-1920-80.jpg
✅ You want an affordable, compatible CPU tower with a display: Compatible with practically all RAM kits imaginable, with exceptional performance, and a display as standard, all for sub $100. Nice.
❌ You're running hotter chips: It's solid, but don't expect it to cool your overclocked Core i9 14900K, or AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D. If that's the case you'll still want a beefy AIO behind them.

The software, though, was a challenge on my machine. For whatever reason, Chrome, Brave, and Edge all flagged it as untrusted, and no matter what I tried with Windows, I could not for the life of me get it to download (this is less a problem with Sudokoo, more Microsoft, being, eh, well, Microsoft). In the end, I had to download it on a Linux machine, chuck it on a USB and bring it across that way. The software's fairly barebones, but it gives you all the system stats you need, and hooks up nicely with the SK700V as well.

As for performance. Stellar. Genuinely Stellar. I tested this at an ambient temp of around 26 to 27 degrees C, and it beat almost every other single tower cooler in our testing stack. In Baldur's Gate 3, it beat almost every air tower it went up against, bar Thermalright's Peerless Assassin 120 SE, but demolished everything in Metro Exodus, was pretty good in X264, beaten only by the Thermalright and the Arctic Freezer 36 , not really winning any accolades, but monstered everything in Cinebench R23. A true testament to the design, given it was operating in ambient conditions four to five degrees higher than elsewhere.

The SK700V is, for a first attempt (and I know, yes, it's technically a licensed design), remarkable. At this price point, delivering this kind of performance, it's just brilliant to see. Particularly when the rest of the industry is on such a price hike at the moment, is it perfect? No. But if you're after an affordable air tower that looks good, and delivers while it does it, well, there are few I'd recommend more.

news.title: 《守望先锋》正在将 6v6 角色队列添加到其竞技游戏中：“我们意识到 5v5 和 6v6 之间不一定有赢家”
news.summary: This town is big enough for the both of us.

content.v: If you had told me back in 2019 that I'd actually prefer a 5v5 version of Overwatch instead of the traditional 6v6 in the big old year of 2026 I'd have replied: "I'm still playing Overwatch in 2026?" Regardless, it's a strange revelation for sure (the 5v5 preference, not that I'm still playing Overwatch), but as time has gone on more players have discovered a similar love for the slightly more simplistic mode.

While I prefer 5v5 for its more focused fights, emphasis on individual plays, and overall less cluttered nonsense I do also still enjoy playing a game of 6v6 every now and then. The only issue is that for the longest time the only version available in quickplay and competitive was the 6v6 open queue. This option may offer faster queue times, but with that often brings absolutely zero team cohesion.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/c36oDipF2zxrxYT7Evi5MD-1920-80.png

But teams of four supports and two DPS may be a thing of the past now that Team 4 is trialling a 6v6 role queue for competitive. "There will be three Competitive options of the game available on Day 1 of Season 6: our standard 5v5, Open Queue 6v6, and our Role Queue 6v6 test," game director Aaron Keller says in a blog post . "The 2-2-2 Role Queue Competitive mini season will start at season launch and run for the first four weeks of the season. We’ll also keep the Open Queue version of 6v6 running and the balance patch will be applied to that mode as well."
"There are also some matchmaking changes shipping with Season 6 that we theorise will keep queue times more manageable."
Aaron Keller, game director

Team 4 is also keeping the 6v6 open queue around for scientific purposes, as the devs will use it to help determine whether players queue 6v6 because they love the game mode, or because they love the shorter queue times. The team has already acknowledged that queue times for 6v6 role queue may be a bit lengthy as it'll have to find not one, but two whole tanks per team for a game to start. Although Keller does add that "there are also some matchmaking changes shipping with Season 6 that we theorise will keep queue times more manageable."

Do I think this matchmaking change will solve queue times for 6v6 role queue? Probably not. But if it helps ease it, even slightly, then we may have a winner between 5v5 and 6v6. As many players switched over to the former due to the lack of tanks (and therefore long wait times) for the latter.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PTJNn6U2t7PhpamQWpCfQn-1920-80.jpg

Keller has stressed that this popularity contest isn't about ousting one game mode: "Over the past few years, we’ve realised that there doesn’t have to be a 'winner' between 5v5 and 6v6. The real competition should be in your matches, not between two modes that can coexist. You can play either one (many people actually play both!) and we’re going to support that choice.

"Currently, we don’t have any intention of moving the main mode of Overwatch to 6v6, but we’re starting to think of it as a second among equals. We’ll put more energy into balance patches for the mode and we’ll continue to look for the right format that really gives our community the experience they’re looking for."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/caRV84N5ZG3ShDtZoueqng-1920-80.jpg

Team 4's approach to Overwatch's different game modes is a great example of how to handle a live service game. Instead of forcing a specific game mode onto players, letting the community decide what works best for them by voting with their playtime ensures that players are getting what they want. The only issue I've seen with it is that it whittles out smaller more experimental modes like Stadium, as the playerbase is split between competitive and quickplay and then two, going on three core modes.

I liked Stadium, and was sad to see it go . But as I said before, players vote with their time in Overwatch, and with only 6% regularly choosing Stadium it was clearly not a smart investment for Team 4 to continue putting so much work into it.

Team 4's decision to slowly experiment by bringing back old modes instead of shoehorning them into the game is smart, and will likely make for a better experience in the long run, regardless of if the 6v6 role queue makes it past the first four weeks of Season 6 or not.

"One of the things that I hope you take away from this is that we’re always trying to improve Overwatch in ways that matter to you," Keller adds. "Just don’t start asking for 7v7!" Huh, now you've said it 7v7 could be quite fun.

news.title: 《天际》如何将第二人生打造为一款舒适的游戏
news.summary: 15 years after release, Skyrim's icy, dangerous world feels warm and cozy. But why has this dark fantasy becom

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/11/cozyskyrim-blogroll-1794397242244.jpg

Every few months, some YouTube channel will upload a video essay asking why we continue to play Skyrim more than a decade after release. Virtually all of them come to the same conclusion: at this point, what keeps us coming back for more isn’t the gameplay, or the story, or the seemingly never-ending wait for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel , but the coziness of its setting.

At a glance, this makes perfect sense. After all, many of us no longer play Skyrim to progress the narrative or complete quests, but simply to spend time in its world. And yet, if you really think about it, it’s also kind of strange. Many cozy games are devoid of danger or pressure, and sport a warm, colorful, often cartoonish look. Skyrim, on the other hand, is dark fantasy 101, its lands frozen over and filled with scary, pointy things that can and will kill you if given the chance.

Sure, some use mods that remove enemies, shake up mechanics, and even clear up the weather, making the game look and feel more similar to cozy favorites like Animal Crossing or Stardew Valley . However, I don’t think I’m alone when I say that – to me – the base game already feels incredibly cozy as it is, dragons and all. For many years I’ve wondered why. And this month, in honor of Skyrim’s 15th anniversary, I took a stab at finding answers.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/11/skyrimcozy2-1794395251214.jpg

While researching, it quickly became clear that most of the common reasons for Skyrim’s coziness do not hold up to scrutiny. Yes, the game’s awe-inspiring landscapes and Jeremy Soule’s soundtrack definitely play a role, but I believe it’s only a supporting one. Otherwise, why would I feel a similar kind of coziness playing games like Bioshock or Batman: Arkham City, which look and sound completely different?

“Nostalgia,” you might say, and many do. But that doesn’t quite cut it either. While the world of Skyrim has indeed become like an old friend, and booting up the game reminds me of the carefree teenage years that coincided with my initial playthrough, the coziness I feel today is – for the most part – the same coziness I remember feeling back then.

The nostalgia factor connects to another, and in my opinion equally insufficient explanation: player competence. The more we play a game, the better we get, and the easier, less threatening, and therefore cozier said game should become. Again, not my experience. For me, playing with a heavily underleveled character, so that even the most ordinary enemy encounter becomes an existential threat, actually makes the game feel more cozy, not less. Strange right?

Not really, it turns out. While early reports on the design of cozy games connected coziness to an absence of danger, today we understand the relationship to be a bit more complicated. In an article about the rise of “dark” cozy games like Dredge and Cult of the Lamb , which play around with mechanics that scare, stress, or unsettle, Polish media scholar Agata Waszkiewicz argued that danger and coziness don’t necessarily cancel each other out. Quite the contrary, designers can in fact use one to amplify the other.

“Coziness is a tricky concept to define,” Waszkiewicz tells IGN, “so we often do it by juxtaposing it with something that clearly is not cozy. There’s a reason everyone always talks about being wrapped up in a blanket, drinking tea or hot cocoa, while it is pouring outside. That contrast between outside and inside makes coziness more pronounced and easier to grasp.”

“A cabin feels warm because of the blizzard,” agrees Rachel Kowert, a research psychologist who specializes in games and mental health. The psychology of cozy games make her think of something called Prospect-Refuge theory, which basically argues that people are evolutionarily “drawn to spaces where we can see out over the world while also being sheltered from it.”
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/11/skyrimcozybonfire-1794395368837.jpg

FromSoftware games have clear equivalents of prospect-refuge points in the forms of bonfires, lamps, and sites of grace: locations that shield players from enemies, even when they’re standing right beside you, while also allowing you to level up, replenish resources, and prepare for the journey ahead. Our prehistoric ancestors would have surely been able to relate.

Skyrim may not have bonfires, but its world likewise contains plenty of places where players are in proximity to yet safe from threats. Think of when you’re passing over one of the province’s many mountaintops and see a dragon flying overhead, or a giant herding his mammoths down below. For me, these are precisely the moments when the game’s world strikes me as most peaceful, and Soule’s soundtrack most relaxing.

Mark Teare, an effects artist who has since left Bethesda and is now working on a cozy game of his own, can think of another reason for why Skyrim evokes such strong feelings of coziness in players: ants. Yes, there are ants in this game, and Teare is the one who put them there, despite Bethesda’s initial protests.

“My boss saw them and was like, ‘No one is ever going to see them. Why are we wasting time on this?’” he tells IGN. “But for me they were a big deal, precisely because they were so small. Once you notice them, the world just feels so much bigger. You wonder: how many other things am I walking by and not even seeing?”

This rationale touches on a number of things that are integral to cozy game design, including presence and connection. Cozy games often encourage players to slow down and appreciate things that in other types of games they might overlook or take for granted. Details like Teare’s insects also create a sense of intimacy. Not with other players, but with the developers: “These little details didn’t need to be there, but their presence shows players that we cared, and they feel that.”

Soule once said a very similar thing, stating in an old interview that he wanted the game’s music to be a constant companion. His goal wasn’t to feed into the game’s power fantasy, but make the player “not feel alone” and “like there’s meaning to what they’re doing.” Whether you’re an expert on Elder Scrolls lore or not, his ethereal soundtrack gives you a sense that some or other god is watching over you, and that – despite the chaos of civil war and the coming of Alduin – everything in this world is fundamentally in harmony.

Speaking to Teare, I stumbled upon my third and perhaps most compelling explanation for Skyrim ’s coziness: the fact that Bethesda didn’t intend for the game to feel cozy at all. “I was down in the trenches, so I’m not sure what the big, big plans were,” he says, “but I don’t remember any discussion or mandate or anything, and none of us were actively thinking about coziness while working.”
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/11/skyrim-cozy-1794395268714.jpg

During our conversation, Teare brought up ASMR – a sensation closely related to coziness, and hugely influential to his ongoing projects. While there are lots of successful ASMR content creators out there, many aficionados will tell you that the most potent ASMR is created unintentionally . “When someone is trying hard, it feels manufactured,” says Teare. In his opinion, the best “ASMRtists” are “really good actors” that make what they’re doing seem natural even though it’s not.

news.title: 光荣的GMMK永恒评论
news.summary: A solid, fuss-free step-up mechanical keyboard.

content.v: It seems Glorious is intent on converting you out of that old Amazon Basics keyboard you might have sat on your desk and into something with a little more of, well, everything. The new GMMK Eternal is the second product in the brand's seemingly entry-level line of peripherals after the excellent Glorious Model O Eternal gaming mouse I tested a few months back. If that's anything to go by, this is a keyboard that homes in on the fundamentals to make for a solid step-up mechanical product.

The brand's own marketing materials focus on all the compromises you potentially make by going for a more affordable keyboard, such as a case that sounds like a biscuit tin, or even simply a sacrifice for a smaller layout. The GMMK Eternal aims to provide a magic bullet to all of the ailments to save you from, at best, a dissatisfactory keyboard that was at a tempting price in a sale.

The 96% layout the GMMK Eternal opts for provides virtually all of the functionality you could ask for. It squishes up the number pad and moves the nav cluster on top of it to provide a full-size keyboard in a reduced footprint to make for one of the easier abnormal key layouts to get used to.

Physical touches otherwise include some doubleshot keycaps with a pleasant texturing to them to aid grip under finger. I am quite sad to report they're ABS rather than PBT, though. This is a marker of a cheaper keyboard, even though PBT has made its way down the price ladder to more wallet-friendly options in recent years, such as the Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 . That said, I'm a fan of the side-printed legends on the function row for quick access to media controls, hotkeys for a calculator, web browser and more, plus access to RGB backlighting level and different patterns.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/BsVKZev3egYL2T5nskS8T7-1920-80.jpg

Switch type: Glorious Fox Keycaps: ABS, doubleshot Lighting: RGB, controllable in software and on keyboard Onboard storage: 3 profiles Extra ports: None Connection type: Wired USB-C Cable: USB Type-C/USB Type-A, detachable Weight: 886 g/1.95 lbs Price: $100 / £90

You don't get any additional extras such as a rotary encoder for volume or any form of toggle switches for OS selection, though. The rear side has a set-in cut-out for a USB-C cable, and the underside has some grippy two-stage feet to raise the angle of the GMMK Eternal up. Otherwise, that's about it.

I'm happy to report that, as much as the frame of this keyboard is virtually all plastic, build quality is largely okay. There's a good amount of heft to the chassis and no deck flex to speak of thanks to an aluminium top plate—Glorious has at least put some thought into making a keyboard that's not flimsy.

My only issue here is the aesthetic it has opted for—the open housing and all-black look gives the GMMK Eternal more of a dated aesthetic that takes me back to when this was the standard look for a 'gaming' keyboard. Rather, it'd have been pleasant to see a closed housing or some different colours used to differentiate this from a more non-descript finish. There's barely even a Glorious logo anywhere, apart from underneath where you can't see it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Rd4HD3XpTuyW37Ae23S6T7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VmDDLuJTTUvrBXgMK4qfS7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/e7QZh4QEKfGTBUUV3jUET7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/uJLAxPkc8dy4ToNAYX3JT7-1920-80.jpg

Inside, Glorious has stuck with its tried-and-tested Fox linear switches that have been kitted to its mechanical keyboards for some time. They're Cherry MX Red clones, so come with a light and linear 45g keypress and are pre-lubricated for a smooth feel and to aid this keyboard's acoustics. For the most part, I've had no issues with these switches, as they offer decent consistency across the keyboard and it's decently easy to get up to speed with them. It is the only default switch option, though, while rivals from Ducky and Keychron offer a degree of choice out of the box with different weights and feels.

If, for whatever reason, those switches aren't to your taste, though, then as the GMMK Eternal is hot-swappable and is compatible with 3- or 5-pin MX-style options, you can change the switches out with the bundled keycap and switch puller and add in a completely different set with ease. I had some spare Cherry MX Falcon tactile switches left over from a different project, which I slotted into this Glorious keyboard, and swapping them in was a doddle, as it usually is with these keyboards, and it changed the feel to a heavier, tactile finish that I much prefer.

To help its enthusiast credentials, this board also comes with a range of foam and such inside for sound dampening for three total layers, and there isn't any case rattle or ping in my experience. This is one area Glorious makes a lot of in its marketing bumf, so I'm pleased to report it sounds excellent.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/w4eTzgT2kM6vjpLk3bNrS7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VmDDLuJTTUvrBXgMK4qfS7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/F6X5ZrxiBhWZTWSgduZ8S7-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/strdhbnYFDCmLCkEayHyF7-1920-80.jpg
✅ You want a no-nonsense, well-built mechanical keyboard: The GMMK Eternal provides a fuss-free experience that sounds great out of the box and is easy to customise with hot-swappable switches.
❌ You want more quality touches: By spending a little more, you can get extras such as higher-quality PBT keycaps, wireless connectivity and a less plasticky chassis.

Software powers are handled by Glorious Core, which has seen a bit of an overhaul in recent times compared to what it used to be with older Glorious keyboards, such as the GMMK 3 HE . Admittedly, the customisation on offer is quite basic, with the usual key remapping and RGB lighting configuration on a per-key basis, but that's about it. It gets the job done, I suppose.

This leaves me with one key thing to mention—price. The GMMK Eternal is £90/$100, putting it in quite a competitive market sector. At this kind of price tag, we've got the Ducky Zero 6108 , which adds wireless flexibility, PBT keycaps and genuine Cherry MX2A switches to the party. It sacrifices on software, though. A little up the price ladder is the new Keychron K8 Ultra 8K , which offers an aluminium chassis, PBT keycaps, solid wireless connectivity and clever software.

All of this has the potential to put the GMMK Eternal in a bit of a difficult position, although it holds its own for those who want a fuss-free mechanical keyboard that nails the basics. Okay, it could be wireless and a little more stylish, but for the most part, I don't know if enough people would care too much.

news.title: 从服务器芯片的外观来看，AMD 的 Zen 6 游戏 CPU 可能绝对是怪物，并且有一个 3D V-Cache 变体值得关注
news.summary: A tantalising tease.

content.v: AMD has revealed a substantial amount of detail on its next-gen Zen 6 CPU architecture, in the form of a technical deep dive on its newly-unveiled EPYC "Venice" range of server chips.

These models will find themselves buried deep within data centers, but the Zen 6 architecture itself looks extremely promising for next-gen Ryzen desktop processors—and quite possibly, your next gaming CPU.
AMD Zen 6 CPU architecture

Current Zen 5 CCDs with full-fat performance cores max out at eight cores per chiplet, but a single Zen 6 CCD, based on TSMC’s cutting-edge N2P node, is stuffed with 12 of the beasties—alongside 4 MB of L3 cache per core, the same as Zen 5. That adds up to a total of 48 MB of L3 cache per CCD, as opposed to the 32 MB you'd find on an 8-core Zen 5 chip (via Techpowerup ).

A current gen Zen 5 CPU with more than eight cores has to spread them across two CCDs, which can result in latency as the two communicate with each other during multi-threaded tasks. With the upped core count per CCD, a 12-core Zen 6 chip would face no such performance penalty.

It's the "c" core counts that have received the biggest jump in density, though. These aren't the same as Intel's Efficiency cores, instead amounting to scaled down performance cores designed to take up less die space and spread the workload during heavily multi-threaded tasks.

In the case of Zen 6c, 32 cores can be squeezed onto a single core complex, double that of a Zen 5 equivalent. The L3 cache per Zen 6c core has been upped, too, from 2 MB per core to 4 MB. That means a fully-stocked 32-core Zen 6c complex ends up with a stonking 128 MB of L3 cache to play with, quadruple that of a maxed-out Zen 5c version.
Zen 6 speeds

In terms of clock speeds, the full-fat Zen 6 cores on a Venice server chip have a maximum clock frequency of 5.3 GHz, while the Zen 6c cores top out at 4.1 GHz. Rumours suggest the eventual Zen 6-based Ryzen desktop chips will top out much higher than that , potentially above 6 GHz, although we'll have to wait and see in that regard.

AMD has also improved Zen 6's branch prediction, with optimized prediction tables and larger prediction queues, while the return address stack has also been buffed from 52 to 64 entries, alongside two branch predictions per cycle. In essence, Zen 6 should be better at anticipating instructions, and should also recover faster from errors. The reorder buffer, integer physical register, and operation cache sizes have been increased, too.

AMD claims up to a 27% increase in Zen 6's instructions per clock (IPC) performance compared to Zen 5 in certain server workloads. That's a pretty massive uplift, and could bode well for whatever consumer chips we end up receiving based around the architecture.
3D V-Cache

Speaking of which, I'd imagine many of you are curious about the addition of AMD's all-singing, all-dancing 3D V-Cache to this potent new design. Well, one of its new Venice chips is called the Venice-X 9006X SP7, and variants go all the way up to 96 cores with 1152 MB of L3 cache. That's 144 MB of L3 cache for every 12-core CCD, which works out at 48 MB of traditional cache alongside 96 MB of stacked 3D V-Cache.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/UZf4p7JE3uqji82cC3Eqe9-1920-80.jpg

To put that into perspective, the eight-core Ryzen 7 9800X3D (our best gaming CPU pick, no less) has 96 MB of L3 cache in total, with 64 MB being made up of 3D V-Cache. And that's a beastly gaming chip. Many games enjoy the benefits of all that cache sitting so close to the cores, so the prospect of a 12-core successor with 144 MB of L3 cache sitting on board is enough to give me the vapours.
And with no latency penalty between those cores in multithreaded loads, and a potentially hefty performance increase across the board? Mercy, that'd likely be a very impressive gaming chip.

As for when we might see Zen 6-based Ryzen desktop CPUs? Well, this launch is purely focussed on EPYC server implementations, which are beginning to ship now, so exact dates for consumer chips remain to be seen. It seems likely at this point that we might be looking at a first-half of 2027 release, although with everything going on at the moment and a new production process to contend with, all I can really do is speculate.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/h3WffBZqLEKCyYMZBMjPB3-1920-80.jpg

And while we're talking about new CPUs, there's always Intel's upcoming ( and if you believe the rumours, even faster ) Nova Lake chips to keep your eye on. Intel's first 18A-P client chips are reportedly on track for a CES 2027 reveal , which happens in January. It's been a while since we've seen a clash of the CPU titans, so keep your eyes peeled around that time.

Still, AMD's new architecture looks mightily impressive on paper. Given all the hubbub and bad news surrounding PC hardware this year, perhaps some new, ultra-speedy processors are a hope I can cling to going into 2027. Until I see the eventual pricing, I would imagine.
Aw. I made myself sad.

content.v: Play the prologue and chapter one.

Saber Interactive is letting you sample the opening moments of Hellraiser: Revival via a new PS5 demo that's been put on the PS Store today. This isn't one that's tied to PS Plus Premium ; it's a free download for everyone.

You'll get to play through the game's prologue, and then a "portion" of the first chapter. This means you'll get to see a lot of what the title is all about: gore, action, sex... and more gore. content.v: 11月11日，多家品牌足金饰品克价全线大跌，每克降幅为24—31元。周大福、金至尊、六福珠宝、周生生、老凤祥、老庙黄金等品牌金饰价格跌至1200元/克关口，拉长时间来看，多品牌金饰价格较年内超1700元/克的高位大跌约500元/克。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/11/small_202611112120582451.png
周生生足金饰品报1212元/克，较昨日跌31元；周大福足金饰品报1215元/克，较昨日跌24元；老庙黄金足金饰品报1208元/克，较昨日跌25元；老凤祥足金饰品报1211元/克，较昨日跌25元。
金价下跌的主要原因在于美国10月通胀数据全面超预期，10月CPI环比上涨0.4%（高于预期0.3%），核心CPI环比上涨0.3%（高于预期0.2%）且连续第三个月维持在0.3%的高位。

news.title: 双11"大促变大涨" 消费者反应加购物车后反而更贵
news.summary: 一年一度的“双十一”购物季又来了，不少消费者早早将心仪商品加入购物车，就等大促开启后以更低的价格入手。

content.v: 一年一度的“双十一”购物季又来了，不少消费者早早将心仪商品加入购物车，就等大促开启后以更低的价格入手。然而，有消费者发现，自己等来的并不是降价，部分商品在促销期间反而比平时更贵。
据媒体报道，消费者刘丽早在10月份就将一台1.5匹空调加入购物车，准备等到“双十一”促销时下单。当时这款空调叠加国补后的到手价为1835元。
https://img1.gamersky.com/image2026/11/20261111_zy_red_164_19/1164.jpg
然而大促正式开启后，她发现同一个商品链接、同一个型号的空调，国补后价格反而涨到了2166.65元，比此前贵了331.65元。面对消费者提出的价格疑问，商家明确拒绝改价。
类似情况并非个例。消费者顾琦在“双十一”前看中一条售价180元的牛仔裤，原本也打算等大促开启后再购买。没想到活动开始后，这条牛仔裤不叠加优惠券的价格涨至231元，即便使用优惠券，到手价仍为195元，比促销前还贵15元。看到价格变化后，她没有再与客服沟通，而是直接放弃购买。
https://img1.gamersky.com/image2026/11/20261111_zy_red_164_19/1391.jpg
“双十一”原本是消费者集中等待优惠的购物节点，但如果商品在活动前先涨价，再通过优惠券、满减等方式制造降价效果，不仅会削弱消费者对大促的信任，还可能涉及价格违法问题。
业内人士指出，商家“先涨价后降价”是否构成价格欺诈，需要结合实际情况判断。如果商品不存在成本明显增加等合理原因，商家只是为了制造优惠幅度较大的假象而提前抬高售价，随后再以“降价”“打折”等方式促销，具有明显欺骗、诱导消费者交易的性质，就可能涉嫌价格欺诈。
按照相关规定，商家开展促销活动时，应当清晰、准确地展示与价格有关的信息。如果在涨价后再降价的过程中故意模糊原价概念，或者无法提供相应交易记录等材料证明所谓“原价”真实存在，也可能面临价格欺诈的认定风险。
https://img1.gamersky.com/image2026/11/20261111_zy_red_164_19/1710.jpg

news.title: 《GTA6》锁30帧主因是CPU瓶颈！不是光追的锅
news.summary: 即便是性能更强的索尼PS5 Pro，《GTA6》目前也只能以锁定30 FPS的帧率运行。对此，不少玩家将性能妥协归咎于Rockstar采用了光线追踪…

content.v: 即便是性能更强的索尼PS5 Pro，《GTA6》目前也只能以锁定30 FPS的帧率运行。对此，不少玩家将性能妥协归咎于Rockstar采用了光线追踪技术。不过，知名业内爆料人RedGamingTech（RGT）对此给出了不同解释。他认为，《GTA6》在PS5和Xbox Series X|S上无法实现60 FPS，主要原因并非光追，而是主机CPU性能不足。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/11/small_202611112104493101.png
RGT在社交平台X上发文表示，《GTA6》拥有一个规模“极其庞大”的开放世界，其中充满了大量NPC以及各种游戏系统，这些内容都会给CPU带来沉重负担。PS5和Xbox Series系列主机的CPU不仅需要处理物理运算、AI、游戏基础代码，还要负责渲染线程等任务。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/11/small_202611112104327741.png
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/11/small_202611112104335924.png
考虑到PS5、PS5 Pro以及Xbox Series X|S均采用基于AMD Zen 2架构的8核心处理器，而这一架构如今已经相对老旧，因此运行《GTA6》这样的游戏，对现代主机而言并非易事。
因此，主机处理器性能不足，很可能才是Rockstar选择将《GTA6》主机版帧率锁定在30 FPS的主要原因。
遗憾的是，在如今响应速度更快的现代显示设备上，30 FPS画面的观感可能更加明显。对于希望以更高刷新率体验游戏，获得更清晰的画面、更流畅的操作以及更低输入延迟的玩家来说，恐怕只能等待《GTA6》PC版推出。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/11/small_202611112105012494.png

news.title: 由于GDDR7显存成本飙升 RTX 5080 24GB在国内被取消
news.summary: 据最新供应链泄露消息称，英伟达已放弃原定于2027年1月在中国发售的GeForce RTX 5080 24GB显卡。据称，3GB GDDR7显存模块价格过高是导致英伟达放弃该计划的原因，转而继续销售现有的16GB版本。据

content.v: 据最新供应链泄露消息称，英伟达已放弃原定于2027年1月在中国发售的GeForce RTX 5080 24GB显卡。据称，3GB GDDR7显存模块价格过高是导致英伟达放弃该计划的原因，转而继续销售现有的16GB版本。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261111/1794401992_732047.webp
据报道，传闻中的GeForce RTX 5080 24GB显卡已在国内被搁置，据称该公司已放弃原定于2027年1月发售的计划。日媒Gazlog转载了中国硬件论坛博板堂上的一篇帖子，该帖子称英伟达已将此决定通知其独立显卡（AIB）合作伙伴，但并未提供新的发售时间。
该报道将取消24GB版本的原因归咎于3GB GDDR7显存模块的高昂成本。据报道，这些模块的价格约为现有RTX 5080所用2GB模块的三倍，使得24GB配置难以以合理的价格销售。据悉，英伟达将继续采购2GB GDDR7模块，并保留RTX 5080 16GB作为其在中国市场最高端的GeForce产品。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261111/1794402001_896590.png
有趣的是，这与Board Channels此前的说法截然相反。10月下旬，该媒体曾暗示英伟达正在加速RTX 5080 24GB显卡的发布，提前至2026年12月或2027年1月，同时逐步停止16GB版本的生产。
无论如何，RTX 5080 24GB版本目前仍处于不确定状态，而其16GB版本很可能是目前你能买到的最强大的英伟达显卡。RTX 5090对于大多数游戏玩家来说遥不可及，尽管你或许有极小的机会通过英伟达的赠送活动获得一块。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/thumbnews/20260720/1784518943_551412.jpg

news.title: 前 BioWare 开发者表示，克莱尔·奥布斯库 (Clair Obscur) 仍能拯救《质量效应》：Expedition 33 掌握关键
news.summary: The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/17/me1-blogroll-1786972844387.jpg
The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.

In the days since EA announced it was shutting down its storied RPG game studio and killing its in-development Mass Effect Universe project, discussion has turned to the costs behind creating another AAA-budget entry in BioWare's space opera series, following a report that EA decided to invest in Star Wars instead .

Last week, BioWare co-founder Trent Oster suggested that EA would likely have been on the hook for at least $200 million in development costs to finish Mass Effect Universe at a level that fans expected.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200m+," Oster wrote on X/Twitter. "That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work." (To be fair, there is still that Mass Effect TV series in the works. And there certainly won't be any bigger plan in place for the IP if its flagship next game is cancelled.)
Now, Mass Effect lead programmer Christina Norman has said the game could be made for around $50 million — a figure that is five times the budget spent by the makers of Clair Obscur.

Highlighting a report on the French-made RPG's overall budget, which was pegged at less than $10 million, Norman wrote on X/Twitter that this was "a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million.
"I mean 5x the budget of Claire obscure expedition 33 should be more than enough," she continued. "You can always spend more but clever small teams can get it done."

Norman spent more than six years at BioWare working on the original Mass Effect trilogy, firstly as a lead programmer responsible for creating the franchise's conversation system, before moving on to become lead designer for Mass Effect 2 and 3, working to improve the series' gameplay.

In the years since, Norman served stints at Riot Games and her own co-founded startup, before becoming a full-time machine learning engineering consultant focused on LLM-directed character conversations. Still, there's no suggestion that LLM technology would be needed to turn in Mass Effect Universe on a smaller budget.

Even Oster has said he believed a new Mass Effect could be made for "cheaper" than $200m, though it "wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept," he wrote in a follow-up post. Alas, Oster also highlighted another big blocker to a new Mass Effect being made — that EA still owns the franchise's rights, and may never want to give them up, even if it's not actively using them. "The big push would be getting the IP free," he concluded. "The fans deserve more."

Last week's annual N7 Day celebration of the Mass Effect franchise featured the Normandy's cast and crew teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect . This followed an array of footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect Universe appearing online, and a petition for EA to reconsider its decision which has gained more than 325,000 signatures . A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week.

content.v: 《GTA6》定于11月19日登陆PS5、PS5 Pro与Xbox Series X|S，Rockstar已宣布主机版《GTA6》将锁定在30帧运行，性能更强的PS5 Pro也不例外。RedGamingTech认为，造成这一限制的主要瓶颈可能是主机CPU，而非光线追踪。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261111/1794401376_799030_jpg_r.jpg
即使在索尼PS5 Pro 上， 《GTA6》也只能稳定在30帧。许多玩家将性能损失归咎于使用光线追踪技术。知名硬件爆料人RedGamingTech解释说， 《GTA6》在索尼PS5和Xbox Series X|S主机上只有30帧，更多是由于这些主机的CPU性能较弱，而非光线追踪技术本身的问题。
RGT在Xbox上撰文指出，《GTA6》拥有一个“极其庞大”的 开放世界 ，其中充满了NPC和各种系统，对CPU的要求极高。PS5和Xbox Series的CPU需要处理“物理引擎、AI、游戏代码以及渲染线程”。考虑到PS5、PS5 Pro和Xbox Series X|S的8核CPU均基于老旧的AMD Zen 2架构，《GTA 6》在现代主机上运行起来并不轻松。
因此，主机处理器性能不足很可能是R星将GTA 6在主机平台上的帧率锁定在30FPS的主要原因 。遗憾的是，30 FPS的游戏画面在现代显示器上，尤其是在像素响应速度快的显示器上，看起来并不流畅。想要在高刷新率下体验清晰画面、流畅游戏和低输入延迟的玩家，恐怕只能等待GTA 6的PC版本了。
